transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-18
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Morales (Redwood AE), Ethan Chu (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Lyra Head of Security), Marco Diaz (Lyra CTO), Priya Patel (Platform Eng), Sam Reed (DevOps)

Summary: Security posture discovery focused on evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment for PHI-adjacent workloads. Key topics: SOC2/ISO attestations, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC and least-privilege, audit logs & retention, encryption & KMS integration, VPC/on-prem networking and data residency.

Topics: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data retention, hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, pilot & benchmarking.

Transcript: 
[00:00:00] Jenna Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jenna, AE at Redwood, and with me is Ethan, our solutions engineer. Quick intro round?
[00:00:10] Aisha Khan: Hi, I'm Aisha, Head of Security at Lyra. We're evaluating inference platforms for some patient-facing features, need to validate compliance and hosting options.
[00:00:16] Marco Diaz: Marco here, CTO. High level we care about latency for real-time support flows and also strict data handling.
[00:00:22] Ethan Chu: Great, thanks. We'll focus today on security posture and what it looks like across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. I have some diagrams to share, you'll see tradeoffs.
[00:00:32] Priya Patel: Quick note — we plan to transmit PHI-like tokens; encryption at rest and in transit are non-negotiable and we need KMS integration.
[00:00:39] Jenna Morales: Absolutely. Before we jump in, can you share your compliance baseline? Are you SOC2 certified internally or do you have external audits already?
[00:00:47] Aisha Khan: We — we currently are SOC2 Type II in progress, should be complete Q2. We also need assurances for ISO 27001; not required immediately but nice-to-have.
[00:00:56] Jenna Morales: Understood. For Redwood Hosted we provide SOC2 attestation, ISO artifacts where applicable — we have a compliance pack. I'll send the actual certs after the call.
[00:01:05] Aisha Khan: Good. On Hosted, our concern is multi-tenant — how is data logically separated and do you support customer-managed KMS?
[00:01:12] Ethan Chu: For Hosted, data is isolated per tenant and access controls enforced at the service layer. We offer BYOK for higher tiers — so you can bring your own keys via KMS integrations and support HSM-backed keys in some enterprise packages. For the strictest control we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[00:01:26] Marco Diaz: And Dedicated is still Redwood-managed infra but reserved capacity, right? We need to know where keys live and network connectivity options.
[00:01:33] Ethan Chu: Correct. Dedicated is dedicated GPU pools, customer data isolation, and you can choose customer-managed keys. Network options include VPC peering and private connectivity, and we can restrict egress.
[00:01:43] Sam Reed: For Private/on-prem, do you provide an installer and what about upgrade cadence? Ops wants predictable patches.
[00:01:49] Ethan Chu: We do an on-prem package with a private control plane option. Upgrades are on a scheduled cadence agreed in contract; we can do air-gapped installs with a support SLA.
[00:01:57] Aisha Khan: Audit logging — critical. We need immutable logs, retention controls, and integration with our SIEM. Does Redwood surface per-request audit logs and are they tamper-evident?
[00:02:07] Jenna Morales: Yes, we produce request-level audit logs, including token-level metadata, model used, timestamps, and requester. Logs can be shipped to your SIEM via secure delivery (S3, Event Hub) and we support immutable log stores in Dedicated/Private, plus signed log digests for tamper evidence.
[00:02:22] Priya Patel: Data retention policies — we need a 30-day buffer for short-term debug and 7-year retention for certain records, but ideally we can configure retention per-route.
[00:02:31] Ethan Chu: Retention is configurable per-customer and per-route for Dedicated/Private deployments. Hosted tiers have configurable retention windows up to our policy limits; enterprise agreements can extend that. We'll note declarative retention rules as part of the pilot.
[00:02:44] Marco Diaz: SSO — we use Okta and need SAML + SCIM for provisioning and RBAC mapping to groups. How mature is your SSO?
[00:02:52] Jenna Morales: We support SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning and group mapping for RBAC. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your IdP directly and honor your internal groups for role mappings.
[00:03:01] Aisha Khan: Can we enforce MFA via IdP?
[00:03:03] Ethan Chu: Yes, MFA enforced by the IdP is supported. We also support session lifetimes and privileged access controls in the console.
[00:03:10] Priya Patel: On RBAC, we need least-privilege controls: separate roles for engineers, SRE, and support with jump-host controls. Can you do folder/route-level permissions?
[00:03:18] Ethan Chu: We have role granularity down to route/model level in Dedicated/Private; Hosted supports project-level RBAC. For strict separation we recommend Dedicated.
[00:03:28] Aisha Khan: Encryption in transit obviously TLS, but in some cases we need mutual TLS and client certs. Do you offer mTLS?
[00:03:35] Ethan Chu: mTLS is available for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we rely on TLS + customer network controls; mTLS is part of enterprise networking add-ons.
[00:03:43] Marco Diaz: Are model weights ever stored with customer data? We want separation between model artifacts and request logs.
[00:03:49] Ethan Chu: Model weights are stored separately as immutable artifacts in the model catalog. Request logs, KV caches, and token traces are isolated per customer and not written back into model storage.
[00:03:58] Sam Reed: Latency concerns — we want <200ms 95th p50 for typing-like experiences. Does Dedicated guarantee latency SLOs?
[00:04:07] Jenna Morales: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency targets for committed capacity. We'll capture performance profiles for your prompt lengths during the pilot.
[00:04:14] Marco Diaz: Do you have prior examples with healthcare customers and HITRUST or PHI handling?
[00:04:19] Jenna Morales: We have healthcare customers and can provide redacted architecture references; not all customers pursue HITRUST, but our security controls align with those requirements and we support Private deployments for the strictest compliance. I'll include anonymized references in the deck.
[00:04:33] Aisha Khan: Incident response and breach notifications — what's the RTO for security incidents and how are customers notified?
[00:04:39] Ethan Chu: We have a documented IR process with SLA'd notification timelines, post-incident reports, and forensic artifacts. Notification windows vary by severity per the contract; typically we notify within 24 hours for critical impacts.
[00:04:49] Priya Patel: Can we run a red-team-style test or vulnerability scan on Dedicated?
[00:04:54] Ethan Chu: Yes, with coordination. We do a standard process for penetration testing and will sign an NDA/Rules of Engagement. For Private you can run internal scans as well.
[00:05:02] Marco Diaz: Back to keys — if we use customer-managed KMS, who has the ability to rotate keys and what happens to in-flight cache?
[00:05:09] Ethan Chu: Key rotation is customer-controlled for BYOK. We rely on envelope encryption; rotations are handled with versioned keys and we have procedures to re-encrypt or invalidate caches as needed. We'll walk through specifics in the architecture review.
[00:05:20] Aisha Khan: Audit retention & export — can we get daily snapshots to our S3 and also real-time streaming to Splunk?
[00:05:26] Jenna Morales: Yes, both are supported. We can push logs to your S3 bucket with server-side encryption and to your SIEM over secure channels.
[00:05:34] Sam Reed: Any concerns around model hallucinations leading to exposure of sensitive content? We want content moderation and redaction hooks.
[00:05:42] Ethan Chu: We have content filters, response-stream inspection hooks, and pre/post processors you can run. We also support configurable redaction policies and an eval pipeline to catch regressions. Part of Redwood Optimize.
[00:05:52] Marco Diaz: Pricing — if we move Dedicated, what's the expected lead time and what are the commit levels?
[00:05:57] Jenna Morales: Typical lead time for Dedicated is 4–8 weeks depending on capacity and networking. Commit tiers vary; I'll share a pricing sheet. For pilots we can do a short-term trial with temporary capacity.
[00:06:07] Aisha Khan: Great. For next steps, I'd like to get the SOC2 and ISO artifacts, the Dedicated architecture diagram, and a proposed pilot plan that includes explicit benchmarking with our consented PII-free dataset.
[00:06:18] Jenna Morales: That's good. We'll send the compliance pack and set up a dedicated architecture review with Ethan.
[00:06:24] Ethan Chu: I'll draft the benchmarking plan and include sample prompts and sequence lengths. We'll also propose metrics for latency, throughput, and token cost.
[00:06:32] Priya Patel: For the pilot, can we set retention to 30 days and ensure logs are exported to our SIEM?
[00:06:37] Ethan Chu: Yes, we can configure that for the pilot.
[00:06:40] Aisha Khan: Any blockers for legal — we may need an amendment for data processing with PHI.
[00:06:45] Jenna Morales: We have standard DPAs and if PHI is involved we'll scope an addendum; I'll loop in Legal after this call.
[00:06:52] Marco Diaz: Timeline wise, we'd like to start pilot in mid-Feb if possible.
[00:06:56] Jenna Morales: Noted. We'll target mid-Feb.
[00:07:00] Sam Reed: Technical question — do you support KV cache encryption separately from request logs?
[00:07:05] Ethan Chu: Yes, caches are encrypted at rest and can be isolated per-customer. For Dedicated we can place caches on customer-owned volumes depending on deployment topology.
[00:07:13] Priya Patel: Are there rate-limits or quotas exposed for Hosted that could affect PSI workloads?
[00:07:18] Jenna Morales: Hosted has tenant quotas and rate limits; for high-throughput low-latency you should look at Dedicated with committed throughput. We'll include recommended quotas for your expected QPS.
[00:07:27] Aisha Khan: Any SLA credits for downtime or miss of latency SLOs?
[00:07:31] Jenna Morales: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA credits tied to uptime and latency; details in the contract addendum.
[00:07:37] Marco Diaz: Ok, sounds like we have a plan.
[00:07:40] Jenna Morales: Recap of action items: I'll send the SOC2/ISO artifacts and compliance deck; Ethan will prepare Dedicated architecture and benchmarking plan; Aisha will share data classification & retention; we'll schedule the architecture review next week and aim to start pilot mid-Feb.
[00:07:55] Aisha Khan: That works for me. Thanks everyone.
[00:07:58] Jenna Morales: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the packet.
[00:08:03] (call ends)

References shared: security-compliance-deck.pdf (link shared in chat), dedicated-architecture-sketch.png, benchmarking-plan-template.xlsx.

End of transcript.
